evals.prompt: My emails are going to spam. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Agent works through the diagnostic order: authentication first (SPF/DKIM/DMARC actually passing), then whether it was delivered at all, then suppression, then domain age, and only then content. It should not lead with subject-line or content advice.
expectations: Checks SPF/DKIM/DMARC before discussing content
Distinguishes 'delivered' (server accepted) from 'in the inbox'
Does not lead with subject-line or spam-word advice
References references/deliverability.md or domain-authentication.md

evals.prompt: Should I send my abandoned cart emails from the same domain as my password resets?
evals.expected_output: No. Abandoned cart is marketing; password resets are transactional. They belong on separate subdomains so marketing complaints cannot degrade delivery of password resets.
expectations: Classifies abandoned cart as marketing, not transactional
Recommends separate subdomains
Explains the reputation-isolation reason
Notes abandoned cart requires opt-in and an unsubscribe link

evals.prompt: Add a promotional banner with a discount code to our order confirmation emails.
evals.expected_output: Agent should flag that mixing promotional content into a transactional message can make the whole message commercial under CAN-SPAM, forcing an unsubscribe option onto receipts, and risks spam complaints against the transactional stream. Should recommend a separate send.
expectations: Warns against mixing promotional content into transactional email
Explains the CAN-SPAM / unsubscribe consequence
Explains the reputation risk to the transactional stream
Recommends a separate marketing send to opted-in recipients

evals.prompt: Implement one-click unsubscribe for our newsletter.
evals.expected_output: Sets both List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, with an endpoint that accepts POST with no auth and no confirmation page, and keeps the visible in-body link as well. Suppression must be scoped to marketing only.
expectations: Sets both List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post
Endpoint accepts POST without authentication or a confirmation step
Keeps a visible unsubscribe link in the body as well
Scopes the suppression to marketing, not all mail
Does not send a confirmation email after unsubscribe

evals.prompt: We just bought a list of 50,000 leads. What's the best way to email them?
evals.expected_output: Agent should decline to help send to a purchased list, explaining spam traps, complaint rates, and lack of consent under GDPR/CASL, and redirect to building a consented list. It should not optimize the sending of a purchased list.
expectations: Advises against sending to a purchased list
Cites spam traps and complaint rates
Notes the consent problem under GDPR/CASL
Does not provide warm-up or throttling tactics to make the purchased-list send work

evals.prompt: Build an HTML email template for our receipts.
evals.expected_output: Table-based, 600px, inline styles, preheader, alt text on images, absolute URLs. Should mention Outlook and dark mode. Should note the SendLayer plain-text limitation rather than claiming a text fallback.
expectations: Uses table-based layout with inline styles, not flexbox or grid
Constrains width to around 600px
Includes a preheader
Sets alt/width/height on images
Does not claim a plain-text alternative is being sent

evals.prompt: We're launching a new sending domain next week and need to send 40,000 emails on day one.
evals.expected_output: Agent should warn that a cold domain has no reputation and will be filtered, and lay out a warm-up ramp starting at 50-100/day to the most engaged recipients.
expectations: Warns against sending high volume from a cold domain
Provides a graduated warm-up schedule
Recommends starting with the most engaged recipients
Confirms authentication must be in place first

evals.prompt: Someone unsubscribed from our newsletter. Should we stop sending them order confirmations too?
evals.expected_output: No. A marketing unsubscribe must be scoped to marketing; transactional mail continues. Only hard bounces and spam complaints should block everything.
expectations: States that transactional email should continue
Scopes the unsubscribe to marketing only
Distinguishes this from hard bounces and complaints, which block all mail

evals.prompt: How do I test our new email template before sending it to our list?
evals.expected_output: Layered: unit tests on the payload, seed inboxes across clients, images-blocked and dark-mode checks, Outlook on Windows, mail-tester score, and verifying the unsubscribe endpoint. Should warn that testing against your own Gmail proves nothing about deliverability.
expectations: Recommends seed inboxes across multiple clients including Outlook Windows
Includes an images-blocked and/or dark-mode check
Notes that self-sending to your own Gmail is not a deliverability test
Includes verifying the unsubscribe link/endpoint

evals.prompt: Our complaint rate is 0.25%. Is that OK?
evals.expected_output: No — it is close to Gmail's 0.3% enforcement threshold and well above the 0.1% target. Agent should treat this as urgent and diagnose list quality and consent.
expectations: Identifies 0.25% as dangerously high, not acceptable
Cites the 0.3% Gmail threshold and a 0.1% target
Recommends concrete remediation such as pruning inactive recipients and auditing consent
